Worked Examples

Equity funds: Bought for ₹5,00,000 and sold for ₹8,00,000 after 2 years. The gain is ₹3,00,000. After the ₹1,25,000 allowance, ₹1,75,000 is taxed at 12.5%, so tax with cess comes to ₹22,750.

Older property: A resident bought a flat for ₹50,00,000 in FY 2015-16 and sold it for ₹90,00,000 in FY 2026-27. Indexation raises the cost to ₹75,59,055, using an index of 384 / 254. Tax before cess is ₹2,88,189 at 20% with indexation, against ₹5,00,000 at 12.5% without. The indexed route is lower.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the capital gains tax rate on shares in India?
On listed shares and equity mutual funds, gains on holdings of up to 12 months are taxed at 20%. Longer holdings are taxed at 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year. Both also carry 4% cess, and surcharge can apply on high incomes.
How are debt mutual funds taxed?
Debt funds bought on or after 1 April 2023 are taxed at your income tax slab rate, however long you hold them. Older purchases can follow different rules, so check before relying on this calculator for those units.
How is tax on property sale calculated?
Property held for up to 24 months is taxed at your slab rate. Longer holdings are taxed at 12.5% without indexation. Resident individuals and HUFs who bought land or a building before 23 July 2024 can instead choose 20% with indexation, whichever is lower.
What is the Cost Inflation Index?
It is a government index used to raise your purchase cost for inflation. The indexed cost is your cost multiplied by the index for the year of sale, divided by the index for the year of purchase. It is notified as 384 for FY 2026-27.
Can I avoid capital gains tax on selling a house?
You may be able to reduce or defer it by reinvesting in another home or in specified bonds, subject to conditions and deadlines. This calculator does not include those exemptions, so speak to a tax professional before a large sale.
Does this calculator include surcharge?
No. It includes 4% cess, but not surcharge on high incomes, set-off of losses, or the grandfathering rule for equity bought before 1 February 2018. NRIs can also face different rules and tax deducted at source.
